title: The 'Black Swan' That Wipes 50% Of Market Value | Mark Skousen
speaker: Mark Skousen (Oxford Club / Skousen Report)

macro_themes.view: Gross output and B2B spending surged (+13.8% Q2), a leading indicator that GDP will accelerate; consumer sentiment can be ignored.
Inflation is stubborn and in a permanent era; core inflation is a misleading concept, and the Iran war and deficits add to it.
$2T deficits and $7T of rollovers could trigger a no-bid Treasury crisis, forcing much higher rates; a black-swan that could cut stocks 50%, timing unknown.
Admires Warsh as a potential Volcker; to cut rates the Fed must slow 5% money-supply growth and tighten.
Democrats likely win the House, maybe the Senate, on affordability and an unpopular war.

calls.reason: Inflation and rates move together over the long run; deficits and heavy issuance mean investors must be paid more, risking a Treasury crisis.
calls.quote: over the long term uh inflation, the rate of inflation and interest rates tend to move together.
